cards.body:
*Lesson 2.7 · AI Modules & Make AI Agents*

_≈ 110 minutes · with Emeka_

Every supplier sends invoices in a different layout: neat PDFs, phone photos, even handwritten slips. Today Sage reads them all inside a Make scenario, pulls out every line, and Weave checks the arithmetic before anything reaches the books. Then you'll meet Make's AI agents, which decide for themselves which tools to use.

*Your problem:* Invoices and receipts still need typing in by hand.
*The plan:* Use Make's AI modules and agents to read documents and decide what happens next.
*After this lesson:* You can automate document work end to end.

*Five suppliers, five layouts*

*Month-end:* The 1.1 Zap files every invoice in Drive. But someone still types each one into the books: 25 invoices, 3 hours.

*The hard one:* Mama Bisi's farm sends a phone photo of a handwritten slip.

*Glitch:* "One swapped digit. The AI reads it confidently. Nobody checks. Your books are off by ₦9,000."

*The deal:* "I'll read," says Sage. "I'll add up," says Weave. "And anything that doesn't add up goes to Tolu."

*Three ways to use AI in Make*

_Option · What it is · How it's paid for · Best for_
- *Make's built-in AI* · Make AI tools (extract, categorise, summarise…) and the AI Content Extractor for documents, using Make's own AI provider · Credits, including extra credits based on token use · Quick starts with no separate AI account
- *Provider apps* · OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini and others, connected with your own API key · The provider bills tokens; Make charges the module's credit · Control over the model, and predictable token billing
- *Make AI Agents* · An agent with instructions, a model and tools (modules, scenarios, MCP), run from a scenario · Credits for the agent's work plus model usage · Tasks where the steps vary each time

Billing summary from Make's help centre (Oct 2026). Make AI Agents is in open beta: Make's own AI provider works on every plan, while connecting another provider to an agent needs a paid plan. Check current credit usage for AI before quoting a client.

*Structured output in Make*

Same idea as 0.5 and 1.5: the AI must return JSON in a fixed shape. In Make, two habits make it mappable:

- *Use JSON mode or structured output*: if the provider module offers it, so the model is held to valid JSON.
- *Parse it with a data structure*: Add *JSON · Parse JSON* and define a data structure (or generate one from a sample). Now `supplier`, `total` and `lines[]` appear as fields you can map and iterate (2.4).

*Getting text out of documents*

*Text PDFs*

- Generated by software; the text is inside the file.
- Extraction is reliable; any capable model can then structure it.

*Scans and photos*

- Pictures of text. They need OCR (optical character recognition) or a model that reads images.
- Expect more mistakes, especially handwriting. Check harder.

*Privacy check (0.6):* invoices contain supplier bank details and prices. Send only the files you need, use a provider whose API data terms you've read, and never paste invoices into a free chat app to test.

*Rules check the AI*

Invoices carry their own proof: the numbers must add up. Run these rules after every extraction, and only save automatically when all pass:

- *Each line*: qty × unit price = line total (within ₦1 for rounding).
- *The sum*: Line totals add up to the subtotal, and subtotal + VAT = total.
- *The basics*: Supplier, invoice number and an ISO date are present; the supplier is on your supplier list.

*Weave:* VAT in Nigeria is 7.5%, but not every supplier charges it. I flag "VAT isn't 7.5%" as a note for Tolu, not an error. Rules should match how your business really works.

*Make AI Agents*

An agent in Make has a *system prompt* (its job and rules), a *model connection*, and *tools*: Make modules, whole scenarios, or MCP toolboxes. A scenario runs it with the *Run an agent* module; a *thread ID* lets it remember a conversation; it can return structured output; and it can use knowledge files you attach.

*Use a scenario when*

- The steps are the same every time (invoice extraction).
- You need predictable cost and easy testing.

*Use an agent when*

- Requests vary: "How much did we spend on tomatoes last month?" vs "Which supplier raised prices?"
- The agent can pick from safe, read-only tools.
*The invoice checker*
Hands-on lab: The invoice checker. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

Featured video: _How to Use the New Make.com AI Agents App_.
Look for: Agent goals and instructions, and scenarios attached as tools.

cards.body: *Solved problem: invoices into the books, checked*

*Step 1 · Watch the invoice folder*

Trigger: *Google Drive · Watch Files in a Folder* on "Supplier invoices" (the folder your 1.1 Zap fills). Then *Google Drive · Download a File*. Schedule hourly in business hours (2.1).

*Step 2 · Ask the AI for the invoice as JSON*

Use a provider module that accepts files or images (or extract the text first with Make's AI Content Extractor). Prompt:
Code example on screen (Ask the AI for the invoice as JSON): open it in the app.
Then *JSON · Parse JSON* with a data structure generated from the clean sample in the playground.

*Step 3 · Check the arithmetic*

*Iterator* on `lines`, then a *Numeric aggregator* (SUM of line_total, source = iterator). In the same iterator section, a *Set variable* or text aggregator collects any line where `qty * unit_price` differs from `line_total` by more than 1 (2.2 maths in a field). After the aggregators, one *router* (2.3):

_Route · Filter · Action_
- *Auto-save* · no bad lines AND sum = subtotal (±1) AND subtotal + vat = total (±1) AND invoice_number exists AND unreadable_parts is empty · Add rows to Supplier_Invoices and Invoice_Lines
- *Fallback · Review* · anything else · Add to Needs_Review with the reasons and the Drive link; email Tolu

*Step 4 · Protect the AI step*

Add an error handler on the AI module (2.6): alert, then *Break* with two retries. If the provider is down, invoices wait instead of disappearing.

*Step 5 · Test with five real-world layouts*

_Invoice · Type · Expected route (example result)_
- *Farmgate Supplies* · Software PDF · Auto-save
- *Ibadan Onion Co.* · Software PDF, two pages · Auto-save
- *Green Basket* · Scanned PDF · Auto-save
- *Hotel produce co-op* · Photo of printed invoice · Auto-save
- *Mama Bisi Farm* · Photo of handwritten slip · Review (no invoice number, unclear digit)

- *4 of 5* saved automatically (example result)
- *1* sent to Tolu with exact reasons
- *≈ 3 h → 20 min* month-end typing, now reviewing exceptions

*Step 6 · Bonus: an "Ask Weave" agent over the invoice data*

Create a Make AI Agent with this system prompt: _"You answer Tolu's questions about supplier spending using only the tools provided. Never change data. If the tools can't answer, say so."_ Give it one tool: a small scenario that searches Invoice_Lines by supplier, product and date range and returns totals. Run it from a scenario triggered by Telegram messages from Tolu's account only, with the chat ID as thread ID.

*Tolu:*

How much did we spend on tomatoes from Farmgate in October?

*Agent:*

₦540,000 across 3 invoices (FG-0188, FG-0192, FG-0197).

*Why this approach works*

- The AI reads; arithmetic checks prove what it read.
- "null plus a reason" turns guesses into review items.
- Only clean invoices skip a human; exceptions arrive explained.
- The agent is read-only, scoped to one tool, and to Tolu's account.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Saving AI output with no arithmetic check.
- Asking for totals but not line items (nothing to verify against).
- Skipping Parse JSON, so fields aren't mappable.
- Giving an agent tools that can write or delete.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* My invoice robot is "nearly perfect". Five issues to find.

*A:* The books were ₦9,000 off for a month before anyone noticed.
*B:* The AI's answer arrived as one long text field; nothing could be mapped.
*C:* A handwritten slip was saved with invoice number "INV-001", which doesn't exist.
*D:* The "Ask Weave" agent deleted a duplicate invoice row when asked to "clean up".
*E:* A staff member tested by uploading 40 real invoices to a free chat website.

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
*A:* no arithmetic check, so a misread digit went straight to the books.
*B:* no Parse JSON with a data structure after the AI step.
*C:* no "use null, never guess" rule; the model invented a plausible number.
*D:* the agent had a write/delete tool. Give agents read-only tools unless a human approves changes.
*E:* real supplier data in an unapproved tool (0.6). Practise with samples; use the provider API with known data terms.

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): One invoice, one JSON, one check
cards.body:
- Make a sample invoice (a document you type up yourself) and run it through an AI module plus Parse JSON.
- Paste the output into the playground checker and fix your prompt until it passes.

*Done when:*
- The checker says AUTO-SAVE and every field maps in Make.

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): The checked invoice pipeline
cards.body:
- Build the solved scenario end to end with your own five sample invoices, including one photo and one with a deliberately wrong total.
- Record which route each took and why.

*Done when:*
- The wrong-total invoice and any unclear one land in Needs_Review with correct reasons, and clean ones save automatically.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): A read-only spending agent
cards.body:
- Build the "Ask Weave" agent with one or two read-only scenario tools.
- Ask it 10 questions, including two it can't answer from the data.
- Record: correct answers, honest "I can't answer" responses, and credits used.

*Done when:*
- At least 8 of 10 answers match a manual check, both unanswerable questions get an honest reply, and the agent has no tool that changes data.

cards.q: After an AI module returns invoice JSON, what makes its fields mappable in Make?
options: JSON · Parse JSON with a data structure
cards.why: Parse JSON turns text into fields and arrays you can map and iterate.

cards.q: What's the best proof that the AI read an invoice correctly?
options: Line totals, subtotal, VAT and total all add up
cards.why: Invoices contain their own arithmetic. Let rules check the AI.

cards.q: The invoice number is smudged. What should the AI return?
options: null, with a note in unreadable_parts
cards.why: Null plus a reason sends it to review instead of inventing a value.

cards.q: When is a Make AI Agent a better choice than a fixed scenario?
options: When requests vary and the agent can choose among safe tools
When you want the lowest, most predictable cost
cards.why: Fixed steps belong in scenarios; varied questions suit agents.

cards.q: What tools should a first spending-questions agent have?
options: Read-only tools that return the data it needs
Email sending, to reply to suppliers
cards.why: Read-only tools keep an agent's mistakes harmless.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. Make offers built-in AI, provider apps, and AI agents; choose by control, cost and how fixed the steps are.
2. Ask for JSON, then Parse JSON with a data structure.
3. Scans and handwriting need OCR or vision models, and stricter checking.
4. Let arithmetic and rules verify AI output; route doubt to a person.
5. "null plus a reason" beats a confident guess.
6. Agents get read-only tools first, scoped to the people who should use them.

*Lesson 2.7 complete!* _AI Modules & Make AI Agents_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Boss 2, _Boss 2: Receipt-to-Books_.
